Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Depressive symptom scores (CES-D) did not differ between T2DM patients with vitamin D insufficiency and those with normal vitamin D.
Sentence: "There was no significant difference between groups with regard to the indices of blood lipid, liver function, and scores in CES-D and PSQI."
Measured as: CES-D score
Population: 132 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
Intervention: Vitamin D insufficiency (plasma 25(OH)D <29 ng/mL), measured not given
Comparator: Normal vitamin D (25(OH)D ≥29 ng/mL)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 132
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Young Japanese women with high depression scores (alone or together with high unidentified-complaint scores) had lower vitamin D intake than those with low scores.
Sentence: "Our findings indicate that participants with high scores for unidentified complaints, depression, or both had lower intake levels of eicosapentaenoic acid, docosahexaenoic acid, vitamin D, and vitamin B12 than those with low scores, alongside reduced fish and shellfish consumption."
Measured as: depression score (questionnaire)
Population: Young Japanese women in a cross-sectional questionnaire survey
Intervention: Dietary vitamin D intake (assessed by questionnaire)
Comparator: Participants with low depression scores
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are cross-sectional and bear on vitamin D and depression, but one used plasma 25(OH)D in T2DM patients and found no difference while the other used dietary vitamin D intake in young healthy women and found lower intake with high depression scores.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["intervention","outcome_measure"],"detail":"population: T2DM patients (n=132) vs young Japanese women; exposure: plasma 25(OH)D status vs dietary vitamin D intake; CES-D vs unspecified depression questionnaire"}
